R comes with hundreds of built-in functions (`sum()`, `sd()`, `sort()`...), and you can write your own with `function(...)`. The last evaluated expression inside a function is what it returns.

```{=html}
<div class="sm-discuss">
  <p class="sm-discuss-label"><i class="fa-solid fa-comments"></i>Discuss first</p>
  <p>Before you run the code below: water freezes at 0&deg;C and boils at 100&deg;C. What Fahrenheit values do you expect <code>celsius_to_fahrenheit(0)</code> and <code>celsius_to_fahrenheit(100)</code> to return?</p>
</div>
```

Edit the code below if you like, then press **Run Code** to check your answer.

```{webr-r}
celsius_to_fahrenheit <- function(c) {
  f <- c * 9 / 5 + 32
  return(f)
}

celsius_to_fahrenheit(0)
celsius_to_fahrenheit(37)

sapply(c(0, 20, 37, 100), celsius_to_fahrenheit)
```
